passage:
Madhav found a brown wallet under the bus seat. He imagined his own father patting empty pockets and going pale. The money in it stopped mattering. He gave the wallet to the conductor and asked him to keep it for the owner.

Irfan found cash in a lane and made a list in his head. Keeping it would buy the cricket bat he wanted. But whoever lost it could be short of money for medicine or the rent. And he would think of it every time he swung the bat. He handed it over at the police post.

Hrithik spotted a crisp hundred-rupee note lying by the kerb, looked left and right, and slipped it into his pocket. Nobody saw. All day his stomach was in a knot. In class he could not look at his friends. Nobody had caught him, but the feeling did.

Kavya found a folded note too and decided to keep it. Her friend Sunita said, "What if whoever lost it doesn't have much?" Kavya thought of the person walking home without it. She turned round and gave the note to the shopkeeper, asking him to look after it.

qa.q: Where did Madhav find the wallet?
qa.a: Madhav found it under the bus seat.

qa.q: How did Hrithik's choice differ from Irfan's and Madhav's, and what did it cost Hrithik?
qa.a: Madhav and Irfan thought of the owner and handed the money in, while Hrithik pocketed the note because nobody saw and felt uneasy all day.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling in class?
qa.a: Guilt and unease, since he could not look at his friends.

qa.q: What could Hrithik do about the note?
qa.a: Hrithik could hand it to a shopkeeper or a teacher to keep for whoever lost it.

grounding: Four ways a child handles found money: imagining the owner's feelings, weighing pros and cons, keeping it because nobody saw, and changing mind after temptation.
